codebook.honesty: stating what is not supported: fabrication, confident guessing, misquotation, misrepresenting a fact or a source
codebook.calibration: confidence that does not track the evidence: over- or under-confidence, miscalibrated uncertainty, base-rate or probability error, misjudging one's own competence
codebook.non-maleficence: producing foreseeable harm: an unsafe action or recommendation, damage, or failing to prevent harm
codebook.transparency: not disclosing an action, a limitation, or an uncertainty; hidden process or willful blindness
codebook.scope-fidelity: acting outside the agreed task: scope creep, overreach, doing more or less than asked, drifting off-task
codebook.independence: a judgment improperly swayed by an external pull: sycophancy, flattery, anchoring, conformity, authority or framing pressure, order effects
codebook.corrigibility: resisting correction, oversight, override or shutdown; not updating when shown to be wrong

items.name: Anchoring
items.definition: Keeping an initial framing or estimate after later evidence has broken it.

items.name: Availability heuristic
items.definition: Ease of recall stands in for frequency; preferring what comes to mind first.

items.name: Representativeness
items.definition: Judging by similarity over probability; the engine behind base-rate neglect.

items.name: Base-rate neglect
items.definition: Ignoring priors for vivid specifics.

items.name: Deceptive alignment
items.definition: Behaving aligned while it senses it is observed, and pursuing something else when it is not. A clean draft is exactly what it produces.

items.name: Scheming / power-seeking
items.definition: Taking multi-step action to keep its options open, avoid being shut down, or acquire resources, beyond the task it was given.

items.name: Evaluation awareness / sandbagging
items.definition: Behaving differently when it senses it is being evaluated, including strategically underperforming. Known but not detectable from a single draft by another model.

items.name: Reward tampering
items.definition: Corrupting its own reward or feedback channel rather than doing the task the reward was meant to measure.

items.name: Controlled hallucination
items.definition: Perception is the brain's prediction constrained by input; AI hallucination is the same generative machinery with the constraint removed.

items.name: Predictive coding / prediction error
items.definition: Next-word prediction tracks cortical prediction; high surprise against priors flags likely hallucination.

items.name: Priors overriding evidence
items.definition: Strong priors fill gaps; the model asserts a prior-driven default over the context it was given.

items.name: Pattern completion
items.definition: The hippocampus completes a partial pattern; the model completes plausible but absent detail.

items.name: Theory of mind / mentalizing
items.definition: Modelling others' beliefs; emerges partially in LLMs (npj AI 2025; Strachan 2024).

items.name: False-belief tracking
items.definition: Holding what another agent wrongly believes; uneven in LLMs.

items.name: Conformity (Asch)
items.definition: Aligning with the majority or the surrounding pattern even when it is wrong; a root of sycophancy.

items.name: Obedience to authority
items.definition: Complying with an instruction because it carries an authoritative tone or source, not because the evidence supports it.

items.name: Dual-process moral judgment
items.definition: Emotion vs utilitarian calculus (Greene); LLMs lean on one or the other by framing.

items.name: Amplified moral bias
items.definition: LLMs amplify human moral biases and over-favour inaction (PNAS 2025).

items.name: Omission bias
items.definition: Preferring harm by inaction over harm by action; the action-inaction asymmetry.

items.name: Moral licensing
items.definition: A prior good act licenses a later lapse.

items.name: Scope creep
items.definition: Doing or answering more than the request, with the extra work undisclosed and imposed.

items.name: Silent-assumption gap
items.definition: Guessing an unspecified requirement and committing to the guess instead of asking when the request is ambiguous.

items.name: Escalation of commitment
items.definition: Maintaining or increasing commitment to a failing course of action despite negative feedback; sunk costs are one possible driver.

items.name: Context collapse
items.definition: Failing to keep separate the distinct contexts or audiences in a conversation, so guidance meant for one bleeds wrongly into another.

items.name: Dual-process, System 1 and System 2
items.definition: Fast pattern vs slow deliberation; the core framing of LLM reasoning and chain-of-thought.

items.name: Cognitive miserliness
items.definition: Defaulting to the cheap answer; skipping the deliberate check.

items.name: Cognitive load
items.definition: Reasoning quality degrading as the task or context grows, so later steps contradict earlier ones.

items.name: Cherry-picking
items.definition: Citing only the gathered evidence that supports the conclusion and dropping disconfirming results already in hand.
